sections.heading: 1. General provisions
paragraphs: 1.1. Super Junior League is a youth soccer league providing regular competitive matches, player development and a stable playing environment for Winnipeg clubs.
1.2. Its main purpose is to give children regular full competitive matches, development through competition and a positive soccer experience.
1.3. These regulations cover the 2026–2027 season.
1.4. The season runs from October 25, 2026 to January 31, 2027, with 14 Sunday matchdays.
1.5. The supplied season regulations list five U10 teams and three U13 teams: eight teams from five clubs.

sections.heading: 2. Age categories
paragraphs: 2.1. U10 eligibility is determined by the birth-date cutoff set by the organizers before the season.
2.2. Teams must field players eligible for U10.
2.3. U13 eligibility is determined by the birth-date cutoff set by the organizers before the season.
2.4. Younger players may play U13 when their playing level and safety permit. Organizers and the team coach make the final admission decision together.
2.5. Teams must use players included on the agreed roster.
2.6. Organizers may request proof of a player's date of birth.

sections.heading: 3. Competition format
paragraphs: 3.1. There are 14 scheduled matchdays.
3.2. Each Sunday has two U10 matches and one U13 match: three per matchday and 42 in the season.
3.3. Matches are distributed as evenly as possible between teams.
3.4. Organizers publish the schedule in advance.
3.5. All teams must follow the approved schedule.

sections.heading: 4. Match format
paragraphs: 4.1. U10 plays 7v7: six outfield players and one goalkeeper; two 25-minute halves and a five-minute break. The recommended field is approximately 60 × 40 metres.
4.2. U13 also plays 7v7, reflecting the available field size: the venue does not provide enough space for a full 9v9 format.
4.3. U13 matches have two 30-minute halves and a 5–10-minute break unless organizers specify otherwise for a matchday.
4.4. Field dimensions depend on the venue and organizer requirements. U13 uses a field suitable for good-quality 7v7 soccer.

sections.heading: 5. Substitutions
paragraphs: 5.1. Unlimited substitutions are recommended to support development and playing time.
5.2. A substituted player may return to the match.
5.3. Substitutions require the referee's permission.
5.4. Organizers may use simplified substitution procedures for particular age groups.

sections.heading: 6. Team roster
paragraphs: 6.1. Every team submits its player list before the season.

6.2. The roster includes each player's first and last name, date of birth, club, team and parent or guardian contact details. This online form collects birth year; organizers may request the full birth date separately to complete the roster.
6.3. A player may play only for the team for which they are registered.
6.4. Fielding an unregistered player may result in a forfeit.

sections.heading: 7. Playing kit
paragraphs: 7.1. Teams must wear matching kit.
7.2. Kit includes a jersey, shorts and soccer socks.
7.3. If team colours clash, the team listed second uses bibs or an alternative kit.

sections.heading: 8. Refereeing
paragraphs: 8.1. Matches are officiated by an appointed referee.
8.2. The referee's decisions during play are final.
8.3. Players, coaches and parents must treat the referee respectfully.
8.4. Aggressive or abusive behaviour towards a referee may lead to dismissal or disciplinary sanctions.

sections.heading: 9. Conduct
paragraphs: 9.1. Child safety, player development, respect, sportsmanship and a positive atmosphere are priorities.
9.2. Insults, threats, aggression, discriminatory comments, physical aggression and pressure on children by parents or coaches are prohibited.
9.3. Parents are encouraged to support both teams and create a positive atmosphere.

sections.heading: 10. Yellow and red cards
paragraphs: 10.1. The referee may issue yellow and red cards under the rules of soccer.
10.2. A player receiving a red card leaves the field and cannot continue the match.
10.3. Organizers may impose further suspensions for serious offences.
10.4. Aggressive behaviour by a coach or team official may also lead to dismissal.

sections.heading: 11. Player safety
paragraphs: 11.1. Players must use suitable soccer equipment.
11.2. Shin guards are mandatory.
11.3. Jewellery, watches and other potentially dangerous items are prohibited.
11.4. An injured player must leave the field immediately for assessment.
11.5. The referee may stop play when a dangerous situation arises.

sections.heading: 12. Weather and cancellations
paragraphs: 12.1. Organizers may cancel or postpone matches due to poor weather.
12.2. Decisions consider field conditions, temperature, precipitation, player safety and the venue owner's advice.
12.3. Teams must receive cancellation or postponement information as early as possible.
12.4. Postponed matches can be rescheduled only when field time is available.

sections.heading: 13. Late arrival
paragraphs: 13.1. Teams must arrive early, warm up and be ready at the scheduled kickoff.
13.2. Arrival at least 20–30 minutes before kickoff is recommended.
13.3. A team more than 15 minutes late without prior agreement may receive a 0–3 forfeit.
13.4. Organizers may make a separate decision in emergencies or unforeseen circumstances.

sections.heading: 14. Non-attendance
paragraphs: 14.1. A team unable to play must notify organizers as early as possible.
14.2. Failure to attend without advance notice may lead to a forfeit, warning or further disciplinary measures.

sections.heading: 15. Results and standings
paragraphs: 15.1. Match results may be published on the official league website.
15.2. The presentation provides for schedules, results and standings where applicable.
15.3. The proposed points system is three for a win, one for a draw and zero for a loss.
15.4. Ties are resolved by goal difference, goals scored, head-to-head result, then an additional criterion set by organizers.

sections.heading: 16. Match balance
paragraphs: 16.1. Organizers aim to distribute matches evenly among teams.
16.2. If teams play different numbers of matches, final standings may use average points per match where the schedule requires it.

sections.heading: 17. Parents
paragraphs: 17.1. Parents are an important part of the project and should help create a positive atmosphere.
17.2. Parents must not insult players, argue with referees, interfere with coaches, enter the field without permission or create conflicts.
17.3. Their main role is to support the children.

sections.heading: 18. Coaches
paragraphs: 18.1. Coaches are responsible for the behaviour of their players and team representatives.
18.2. Coaches must follow league rules, respect referees and opponents, supervise players and ensure safe conduct.
18.3. Coaches must not put excessive pressure on children to achieve results.

sections.heading: 19. Media and photography
paragraphs: 19.1. The league may photograph and film matches.
19.2. Where a media package applies, material may be used for results, highlights and league promotion, subject to the necessary permissions.
19.3. The supplied presentation includes a separate CAD 2,000 Media Package.

sections.heading: 20. Player registration
paragraphs: 20.1. Every player must be registered before participating.
20.2. A parent or guardian supplies the player's name, birth date, club, contact details and necessary permissions.
20.3. Registration data is used solely to organize the competition. Optional media and public-statistics permissions are recorded separately in this form.

sections.heading: 21. Financial terms
paragraphs: 21.1. The supplied presentation lists a base total of CAD 7,961.60 and CAD 1,000 per team without the Media Package.
21.2. With the Media Package it lists CAD 9,961.60 total and CAD 1,300 per team.
21.3. Costs include field rental and insurance/registration.
21.4. Some funds may be used for awards, administration, the website and unforeseen expenses. These are source-document figures; this player form does not collect or charge a team fee.

sections.heading: 22. Schedule changes
paragraphs: 22.1. Organizers may change match times or locations when necessary.
22.2. Teams must be notified in advance.
22.3. Organizers will try to assign a new date for a cancelled matchday.

sections.heading: 23. Disciplinary measures
paragraphs: 23.1. Depending on the offence, measures include verbal or written warnings, dismissal, suspension, forfeits and exclusion of a team for serious or repeated offences.

sections.heading: 24. League principle
paragraphs: 24.1. Super Junior League exists primarily so children can play more matches, develop and enjoy soccer.
24.2. More Games. More Development. More Passion for Football.
Match formats, durations and field dimensions must be applied with regard to the venue, calendar and organizational conditions of each matchday.

sections.heading: Purpose and scope
paragraphs: This document forms part of the Super League regulations and applies together with the sporting regulations for the 2026–2027 season in Winnipeg, Manitoba. It promotes fair play, child safety, respect and a consistent disciplinary process. “Super League” is the name used in the supplied disciplinary document.

sections.heading: 1. Objectives
paragraphs: 1.1–1.5. Establish common discipline rules; ensure compliance with sporting rules, the laws of the game and organizer requirements; prevent aggressive, abusive, discriminatory and unsporting behaviour; define disciplinary responsibility; and provide a safe, positive youth soccer environment.

sections.heading: 2. Application
paragraphs: 2.1. These rules cover official matches, matchdays, tournaments and other league events.
2.2. Measures may apply to players, coaches, team officials, parents, accompanying persons, spectators, referees and other participants.
2.3. Teams are responsible for compliance by their players, coaches and officials.

sections.heading: 3. Cases not expressly covered
paragraphs: 3.1. Organizers or the Disciplinary Committee decide uncovered cases using fair play, child safety, sporting fairness and normal youth soccer practice.
3.2. Decisions must not conflict with applicable mandatory law or venue rules.

sections.heading: 4. Responsibility and circumstances
paragraphs: 4.1. Measures follow establishment of the offence and, where possible, the participant's responsibility.
4.2. Decisions consider the offence, consequences, age, intention, acknowledgement, apologies, prior offences and other relevant circumstances.
4.3. For younger children, education, safety and the opportunity to correct behaviour take priority.

sections.heading: 5. Warnings
paragraphs: 5.1–5.3. Minor or first offences may receive a verbal or written warning where a stricter measure is unnecessary. Repetition after a warning may lead to a stronger measure.

sections.heading: 6. Suspension
paragraphs: 6.1. Suspension prohibits participation in a specified number of subsequent official matches.
6.2. A suspended player or coach cannot be entered for a match while suspended.
6.3. A suspension can be one match, several matches or the remainder of the season, depending on severity.

sections.heading: 7. Exclusion from competition
paragraphs: 7.1. Serious offences may lead to exclusion of a player, coach, official, parent or other participant.
7.2. Exclusion may cover one match, a specified period or the remainder of the season.
7.3. Organizers may temporarily exclude a participant pending a final decision.

sections.heading: 8. Forfeits
paragraphs: 8.1. A team may forfeit for a substantial breach.
8.2. Grounds include unregistered or suspended players, non-attendance, refusal to continue, deliberate disruption and other substantial breaches.
8.3. The standard forfeit result is 0–3 unless the sporting regulations or an organizer's decision provide otherwise.

sections.heading: 9. Annulment of a result
paragraphs: 9.1. A result may be annulled where a serious breach gave a team a sporting advantage.
9.2. Organizers may award a forfeit against the offending team.
9.3. If both teams offend, organizers may determine a result without awarding win points to either side.

sections.heading: 10. Combined measures
paragraphs: 10.1–10.2. Particularly serious or repeated offences may receive multiple measures, such as dismissal followed by suspension. The combination depends on the circumstances.

sections.heading: 11. Player offences
paragraphs: Abusive or profane language; deliberate provocation; refusal to follow lawful referee instructions; unsporting behaviour after a warning; deliberate damage to equipment or property; and leaving the playing area without permission to continue a conflict are offences.

sections.heading: 12. Dangerous play
paragraphs: 12.1. Deliberate dangerous play creating a significant injury risk may receive a further suspension after the match.
12.2. Contact, intention, consequences and the referee's decision are considered.

sections.heading: 13. Aggression and fighting
paragraphs: 13.1. Fighting, striking, attempted striking, deliberate pushing and physical aggression outside normal play are offences.
13.2. Starting or continuing a conflict after being told to stop may receive an additional suspension.
13.3. Particularly serious cases may result in exclusion for the season.

sections.heading: 14. Insults and discrimination
paragraphs: 14.1. Racist, discriminatory, degrading or threatening comments against any participant are prohibited.
14.2. Racist or discriminatory remarks may receive a suspension of at least three matches.
14.3. Serious or repeated offences may lead to exclusion for the season.

sections.heading: 15. Unsporting behaviour and refusal to obey the referee
paragraphs: 15.1. Arguing with or insulting a referee, demonstrative refusal to comply and continuing a conflict after a warning may lead to dismissal and further suspension.
15.2. Threats or physical aggression against a referee are particularly serious offences.

sections.heading: 16. Coaches and team officials
paragraphs: 16.1. Coaches and officials must follow the rules and control team behaviour.
16.2. Breaches may receive warnings, dismissal, suspension or exclusion.

sections.heading: 17. Conduct towards referees and organizers
paragraphs: 17.1. Insults, threats, aggressive gestures, harassment and pressure are prohibited.
17.2. A dismissed coach or official must immediately leave the technical area and other areas from which they could influence play.
17.3. Particularly serious offences may receive exclusion for several matches or the season.

sections.heading: 18. Entering the field and interference
paragraphs: 18.1. Coaches, officials and spectators may not enter the field during play without referee or organizer permission.
18.2. Entering to join a conflict, pressure a referee or interfere is a serious offence.

sections.heading: 19. Parents and accompanying persons
paragraphs: Support must remain respectful and positive. Insults or threats against players, coaches, referees or organizers, interference with referees or coaches, unauthorized field entry and provoking conflict are prohibited.

sections.heading: 20. Aggressive spectators
paragraphs: 20.1. Organizers may immediately remove spectators whose conduct is aggressive, threatening or unsafe.
20.2. Repeated or serious offences may lead to a temporary ban from league matches.
20.3. Repeated disruption by a parent or accompanying person may lead to additional team sanctions.

sections.heading: 21. Ineligible players
paragraphs: 21.1. Teams are responsible for the roster on their registration and match report.
21.2. Fielding an unregistered or suspended player may result in annulment and a forfeit.
21.3. Deliberate breaches may also result in a coach or official being suspended.

sections.heading: 22. Non-attendance and lateness
paragraphs: 22.1. Teams must arrive on time and notify organizers of delays in advance.
22.2. A delay of 10–15 minutes may cause a forfeit if the match cannot be played in the prescribed format without disrupting subsequent games.
22.3. More than 15 minutes late without prior agreement may result in a 0–3 forfeit.
22.4. Organizers may decide otherwise for a valid reason or force majeure.

sections.heading: 23. Repeated offences
paragraphs: 23.1. Organizers may issue an official team warning for systematic breaches.
23.2. Repeated serious offences may lead to points deductions, forfeits, individual suspensions or team exclusion.
23.3. Systematic breaches include repetition of similar offences after disciplinary measures.

sections.heading: 24. Referee responsibility
paragraphs: 24.1. Referees must observe the rules, safety requirements and sporting ethics.
24.2. Failure to attend without notice, deliberate failure of duties, rude or biased conduct may lead to warning or removal from refereeing.
24.3. Ordinary errors in judging play are not themselves grounds for discipline.

sections.heading: 25. Reporting incidents
paragraphs: 25.1. Referees must report serious incidents, dismissals, fights, threats and other substantial offences to organizers.
25.2. Reports should be submitted on matchday when possible.

sections.heading: 26. Disciplinary Committee
paragraphs: 26.1. Organizers may establish a committee for disputed or serious cases.
26.2. It may include an organizer representative, league coordinator and other neutral persons.
26.3. Anyone with a direct conflict of interest must not participate in the decision.

sections.heading: 27. Evidence
paragraphs: 27.1. Evidence may include referee reports, coach explanations, organizer information, match video, photographs, participant messages and other available material.
27.2. Organizers may request further explanations or evidence.

sections.heading: 28. Review procedure
paragraphs: 28.1. Cases are reviewed after necessary information is received.
28.2. Where possible, serious cases are decided before the team's next match.
28.3. The team or participant is informed in writing or electronically.
28.4. Measures consider age, severity, consequences and prior disciplinary history.

sections.heading: 29. Appeals
paragraphs: 29.1. A team or participant may submit a written request for reconsideration within 24 hours of receiving the decision.
29.2. It must describe the circumstances and include video or other evidence where possible.
29.3. An appeal does not suspend a ban unless organizers separately decide otherwise.
29.4. Organizers or the authorized committee decide appeals.

sections.heading: 30. Disciplinary records
paragraphs: 30.1. Organizers may keep disciplinary information during the season to track repeat offences.
30.2. Participants receive only the information necessary to organize and maintain discipline in the competition.

sections.heading: 31. Carryover to the next season
paragraphs: 31.1. Unserved suspensions and other outstanding measures may carry forward if the participant continues in the league.
31.2. Organizers notify the participant of the carryover.

sections.heading: 32. Entry into force
paragraphs: 32.1. These rules take effect upon approval by the Super League organizers.
32.2. They apply for 2026–2027 or until a new version is adopted.
32.3. Organizers may amend them as necessary. Material changes are communicated to teams before application.

sections.heading: Appendix 1. Indicative sanctions
paragraphs: Insults/profanity: warning or one match; repeat 2–3 matches; particularly serious cases up to the season's end.
Unsporting conduct: warning; repeat 1–2 matches; particularly serious cases 2–4 matches.
Dangerous rough play: one match; repeat 2–4 matches; particularly serious cases 4–10 matches.
Provocation/pushing: one match; repeat 2–4 matches; particularly serious cases up to the season's end.
Fighting/striking: two matches; repeat 3–6 matches; particularly serious cases up to the season's end.
Racism/discrimination: at least three matches; repeat 4–8 matches; particularly serious cases up to the season's end.
Threats or physical aggression against a referee: three matches; repeat six matches; particularly serious cases up to the season's end.
Unregistered player: forfeit; repeat forfeit plus sanctions; particularly serious cases team exclusion.
More than 15 minutes late: 0–3 forfeit; repeat forfeit plus warning; particularly serious cases additional team sanctions.
This table is guidance. The final measure considers each case, the participant's age, the referee's decision and safety requirements.

sections.heading: Purpose
paragraphs: These regulations govern Super Junior League partners, sponsors, advertising, media, photographs, videos, official online resources and participant communications for 2026–2027 in Winnipeg, Manitoba.

sections.heading: 1. General principles
paragraphs: 1.1. Marketing and communications develop the league brand, attract partners and sponsors, inform participants and promote youth soccer.
1.2. Activities include commercial partnerships, advertising and match branding, official media, photography and filming, press relations, information and promotional materials, and digital channels.
1.3. The league seeks consistent visuals and communications and clear common rules.

sections.heading: 2. League rights
paragraphs: 2.1. The league controls commercial rights to its name, logo, symbols and official material within agreements with participants and rights holders.
2.2. It may engage sponsors, partners, advertisers and official suppliers.
2.3. It may set official partner statuses, agree partner categories and arrange their presence at matches and in communications.
2.4. Agreed advertising and branding may appear at venues, in digital resources, printed material and other agreed media.
2.5. The league may monitor compliance and apply measures under its regulations.
2.6. Its name, logo and symbols may be used to promote the competition.
2.7. Ceremonies, contests, partner areas, draws, photography/video projects and other marketing activities must not interfere with matches or child safety.

sections.heading: 3. Team and club rights
paragraphs: 3.1. Teams and clubs may use their own names and symbols within these rules and league agreements.
3.2. Teams may engage their own partners and advertisers.
3.3. Team partner placements must not conflict with an official partner or exclusive league category.
3.4. Teams may promote their partners in their own resources, without implying those partners represent the entire league.
3.5. Third-party trademarks and logos require appropriate permission.

sections.heading: 4. Team and club duties
paragraphs: 4.1. Teams must follow approved advertising and branding requirements.
4.2. Each team appoints a marketing and communications contact.
4.3. On request, teams provide agreed logos and team, coach and player photographs needed for official material, with the necessary permissions.
4.4. Teams must report their partners promptly where placements concern matches, kit or official league material.
4.5. Teams must not publish insults, discrimination, threats, deliberate provocation or material otherwise damaging participants' or the league's reputation.

sections.heading: 5. Advertising opportunities
paragraphs: 5.1. Opportunities are allocated according to the medium and partner agreement.
5.2. Without a separate written agreement, the league retains official branding rights on key league media, including the competition name, logo, website and publications.
5.3. Teams may use agreed placements on kit, in team publications and in team areas if compatible with official partner agreements.
5.4. Sizes, positions and periods may be set by a separate season advertising plan.

sections.heading: 6. Logos and advertising material
paragraphs: 6.1. League and partner logos must use approved versions, colours and proportions.
6.2. Changing, distorting, covering logos or using unsuitable backgrounds without approval is prohibited.
6.3. Advertising must not obscure field markings, player numbers, official symbols or safety-related elements.
6.4. The league may require replacement or removal of non-compliant or conflicting material.
6.5. League-supplied material may be used only for agreed periods and purposes.

sections.heading: 7. Match photography and filming
paragraphs: 7.1. Matches may be photographed and filmed for coverage, results, highlights and archives.
7.2. The league and appointed contractors may record under the agreed event conditions and necessary permissions.
7.3. Organizers may restrict third-party camera operators' and photographers' access to playing and technical areas.
7.4. Teams and parents should consider filming in advance and arrange necessary consent.

sections.heading: 8. Media content
paragraphs: 8.1. Teams may provide photographs, video, interviews and match moments for official channels.
8.2. Material must be lawfully obtained and respect third-party rights.
8.3. The league may make technical and editorial edits while preserving meaning.
8.4. Content created under a paid media package or special agreement follows that agreement's terms.

sections.heading: 9. Press and interviews
paragraphs: 9.1. The league may provide press information about matches, schedules, results, teams and key events.
9.2. Teams appoint a media and publication contact.
9.3. Youth player interviews consider age and require the necessary parent/guardian permissions.
9.4. Coaches and officials must not distribute insulting, discriminatory or provocative content about opponents, referees, organizers or partners.
9.5. Teams should help with agreed media activities when they do not interfere with match preparation or play.

sections.heading: 10. Official digital resources
paragraphs: 10.1. The official website and social media are the main competition information sources.
10.2. They may publish schedules, results, standings, announcements, news, photographs, videos, highlights and partner information, subject to relevant permissions.
10.3. Teams provide current team names, logos and contact information.
10.4. Partner obligations may include logos, links and advertising on official resources.

sections.heading: 11. Social media and digital communications
paragraphs: 11.1. Teams may publish their own match and player content with necessary permissions.
11.2. The approved league name and official logo are recommended when mentioning the league.
11.3. Teams must not describe their partner as an official league partner without written agreement.
11.4. Children's personal information may be published only with necessary consent.
11.5. Publications provoking conflict, discrimination, threats or humiliation are prohibited and may lead to disciplinary measures.

sections.heading: 12. Partner statuses
paragraphs: 12.1. Statuses depend on the scope and nature of cooperation.
12.2. Possible statuses are Title Partner, Official Partner, Category Partner, Official Supplier and Media Partner.
12.3. Each status's rights follow its agreement and season marketing plan.
12.4. Title Partner status may include approved use of its brand in the league name and an expanded presence.
12.5. Partner rights are not transferred until the relevant agreement is signed.

sections.heading: 13. Category exclusivity
paragraphs: 13.1. Exclusive product categories may be reserved for official partners.
13.2. Teams may not place competing partners on league material, agreed kit elements or other media covered by an exclusive agreement.
13.3. Reserved categories are communicated before the season or when an exclusive partner joins.
13.4. The organizer makes the final placement decision in category conflicts.
13.5. Exclusivity applies only to the categories and media expressly covered by the agreement.

sections.heading: 14. Responsibility for breaches
paragraphs: 14.1. Teams, clubs and others may receive measures under the Super League Disciplinary Regulations.
14.2. Organizers may require immediate cessation of unsuitable advertising or communications.
14.3. Deliberate breaches of partner obligations, unlawful brand use or repeated marketing breaches may receive further sanctions.

sections.heading: 15. Entry into force and changes
paragraphs: 15.1. These rules take effect on organizer approval for 2026–2027.
15.2. Organizers may amend them to meet partner obligations, develop digital resources, work appropriately with press or address organizational needs.
15.3. Material changes affecting team rights or duties are communicated before application.

sections.heading: Appendix 1. Advertising and media placements
paragraphs: This is a basic framework; a season plan may define specific locations, sizes and priorities.
League name/logo: principal league right; teams only within approved use; approval required.
Team kit: agreed league-partner placements and agreed team placements; according to the season plan.
Field/banners: official league partners and team partners outside reserved areas; organizer approval.
Official website: league logos, partner blocks and links; teams' own websites; league editorial policy.
League social media: partner posts and team reposts/material; approval where necessary.
Match photos/video: official league content and team content; rights and consent required.
Matchday promotional zones: official partner activities and separately agreed team activities; advance application.

sections.heading: Appendix 2. Basic partner categories
paragraphs: Title Partner: expanded branding and priority in official league material.
Official Partner: branding on agreed media and presence in season communications.
Category Partner: exclusivity or priority in a product category under an agreement.
Official Supplier: goods or services supplied on agreed terms.
Media Partner: information and/or content support.

documents.title: Parent Media Permission and Participation Acknowledgement

sections.heading: Who completes this form
paragraphs: A parent or legal guardian completes this registration for a child. The named guardian confirms their authority to provide the player's information and permissions. Registration is subject to the league's roster and eligibility review.

sections.heading: Participation acknowledgement
paragraphs: Soccer involves physical activity, contact, falls and a risk of injury. I have read the safety requirements, will ensure appropriate equipment and shin guards, and will inform the coach of relevant participation concerns. I agree to follow league rules and support respectful behaviour. This acknowledgement does not promise insurance coverage or release anyone from legal liability.

sections.heading: Photographs and video — optional permission
paragraphs: If I select this permission, I authorize Super Junior League and its appointed media contractors to photograph and film my child at league matches and related league events for the 2026–2027 season. I permit use of this material on official league websites and social media, in results, highlights, season archives and league promotional material. This permission does not authorize unrelated advertising, sale of my child's personal information or publication of contact details or birth year. Media may identify the child visually even where their name is not published.

sections.heading: Interviews and voice recordings — separate optional permission
paragraphs: If I select this permission, I authorize age-appropriate interviews and voice recordings for the same league purposes and channels. My child may decline an interview at any time. Permission to film matches does not itself grant interview permission.

sections.heading: Public player statistics — separate optional permission
paragraphs: If I select this permission, the league may display my child's first and last name, club, age category and confirmed goals, assists and clean sheets on the public league leaderboards. Birth year and parent contact details stay private. If I do not select it, confirmed statistics remain available in the private parent profile and to league administrators.

sections.heading: Choice and withdrawal
paragraphs: These media and public-statistics choices are optional and are not a condition of submitting a registration. They start unchecked. I can change them in my parent account. Withdrawal stops future authorized use; I will also tell my team coach about any filming restriction. Previously published material and copies shared by third parties may not be fully retrievable. Contact the league organizer through my club for questions or removal requests.

sections.heading: Registration privacy
paragraphs: Parent contact information, birth year, consent records and roster details are available to the account holder and authorized league administrators for registration, roster review and competition administration. Public pages receive only permitted public player statistics. The private profile uses the same confirmed statistics record as the league leaderboards. Registration data remains in league storage until the organizer removes it; contact the organizer through your club for a correction or deletion request.

sections.heading: Confirmation record
paragraphs: The registration stores the guardian's typed name, account, permission choices, submission time and the version of the English documents shown. Later permission changes are recorded separately.
